questions.prompt: Why is adding or removing one server at a time safe without a transitional configuration?
options: Because any majority of the old configuration and any majority of the new one must share a server
Because a single new server cannot vote until the change commits
Because servers switch configurations at the same instant
Because the leader pauses all elections during the change
questions.explanation: When the configurations differ by one server, their majorities always overlap, so two leaders cannot be elected in one term even while servers disagree about the configuration. Servers do not switch simultaneously, and new configurations take effect as soon as they are appended, not when committed.

questions.prompt: A leader applies a client's Append, then crashes before replying. The client retries with the new leader. What prevents the Append from being applied twice?
options: The new leader refuses commands that look identical to a recent log entry
The state machine tracks each client's highest applied sequence number and returns the cached result for duplicates
The client waits for the old leader to restart
Raft's Log Matching Property removes duplicate entries
questions.explanation: The duplicate is appended to the log as a new entry, so Raft itself cannot tell. Deduplication lives in the replicated state machine, keyed by client ID and sequence number, so every replica makes the same decision. Log Matching is about consistency between logs, not duplicate commands.

questions.prompt: With ReadIndex, why does the leader send a round of heartbeats before answering a read?
options: To replicate the read as a log entry
To reset followers' election timers so the read is not interrupted
To confirm it is still the leader, so no newer leader can have committed writes it has not seen
questions.explanation: A partitioned leader may not know it has been replaced. Acknowledgements from a majority prove no other leader existed at the time of the read. Resetting timers is a side effect, not the purpose, and ReadIndex deliberately avoids writing the read to the log.
